newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 12.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Thai Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa wants cabinet to see Phuket reports. The prime minister has fuelled a row over the dismissal of the Phuket land reform cases by ordering police interrogation files to be shown to the cabinet today. The move follows Supreme Attorney General Kanit Na Nakhon's dissmisal of the land reform cases last week, a move which provoked widespread criticism. (BANGKOK POST)

- New Aspiration Party (NAP) leader Chavalit Yongchaiyudh yesterday afternoon abruptly cancelled his scheduled campaign speechs in Songkhla and Satun because he wants to focus on forming the next government, a source close to Chavalit said. The source said the NAP would discuss the formation of a coalition government with his party's prospective coalition partners after the Cabinet meeting today. According to the source, in addition to the NAP's current allies, Chat Pattana Party from the opposition camp is expected to join a NAP-led administration. (THE NATION)

- The Public Health Ministry considers importing doctors. Foreign docters could be brought in to ease a shortage here, the permanent secretary of the ministry said. A panel will be set up to look into the possibility and discuss criteria. (BANGKOK POST)

- New Bangkok International Airport Co (NBIA), operator of the Nong Ngu Hao airport project, is expected to seek approval from its board of directors on Nov 18 to terminate the Bt973-million contract with the Murphy/Jahn-TAMS consortium for the design contract which was awarded to the group in 1993 after fierce bidding. A consortium source familiar with US-based Murphy/Jahn said he had also heard of the plan by NBIA to end the contract. (THE NATION)

- American oil firm Amerada Hess was awarded two gas prospective concession blocks in northeastern Thailand. The decision by the company to acquire the blocks was in line with its efforts to replenish its diminishing petroleum production and reserves in the North Sea and the United States. (BANGKOK POST)

- Thailand's Aviation Department says there are now at least six private firms wanting to operate the second airline. The department set November 30 as the deadline for submitting proposals. (THE NATION)
